images.caption: The graveyard can rarely be visited. In it there is the mausoleum for Hüseyin Ağa, who was Kapıağası – Chief of the White Eunuchs under Beyazit II - and transformed the church into a mosque.
images.alt: The graveyard can rarely be visited. In it there is the mausoleum for Hüseyin Ağa, who was Kapıağası – Chief of the White Eunuchs under Beyazit II - and transformed the church into a mosque.

images.caption: The decoration of the old church has gone, but the decoration on the rim under the first floor remains.
images.alt: The decoration of the old church has gone, but the decoration on the rim under the first floor remains.

images.caption: A scanned slide from before restoration changed the appearance of the mosque. On some one can see that formerly floors in mosques used to be covered with individual carpets, often gifted. It gave mosques an appearance that was lost when machine-made carpet took over. One of pictures taken from the first floor, where one gets close to some of the decoration.
images.alt: A scanned slide from before restoration changed the appearance of the mosque. On some one can see that formerly floors in mosques used to be covered with individual carpets, often gifted. It gave mosques an appearance that was lost when machine-made carpet took over. One of pictures taken from the first floor, where one gets close to some of the decoration.

images.caption: The first floor can on occassion be visited, one has fine views, in this case towards the platform to the left, (müezzin mahfili in Turkish) opposite the minbar where the assistant of the Imam, the muezzin, stands during prayer. The muezzin recites the answers to the prayers of the Imam where applicable.

images.caption:
1911 multilingual Ottoman calendar page from Thessaloniki:

The upper left shows the Rumi date in Ottoman Turkish: year 1327, Nisan 7 (٧ نیسان ١٣٢٧)
The same Julian date (7 April, ΑΠΡΙΛΙΟΣ 7) and day (Thursday, Πέμπτη) appears below in Greek with the AD year 1911
Next to that is the Gregorian date (20 April, AVRIL 20) and day (Jeudi) in French
Above these two is the number 30 (twice, purpose unclear probably because the relevant month is 30 days), the month April, (Априлий) and day (Thursday, Четвъртъкъ) in Bulgarian
Under the Greek is Armenian, reading April (ԱՊՐԻԼ, april) and Thursday (ՀԻՆԳՇԱԲԹԻ, hingšabtʿi)
The upper right shows the Islamic date 21 Rebiülahir 1329 (١٣٢٩ ربيع الآخر ١٢)
The Hebrew date 22 Nisan 5671 (22 ‏ניסן‎ 5671) appears at the bottom, mentioning Thursday (in Ladino language) and Pesach (גﬞוגיבﬞיס פסח).
images.alt:
